newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus petrol companies see liquidity squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus petrol companies see liquidity squeeze.

text.p: Cyprus petroleum importers expect losses of up to nine million pounds ($19.5 million) by December because of increases in the price of crude and fixed local prices, industry sources said on Thursday.
"If this situation continues we could have losses of eight million, perhaps nine million pounds by the end of the year," the industry source, who requested anonymity, told Reuters.
The island's six petroleum companies have started contacts with the government over the deficit, which could force a liquidity squeeze on companies by the end of October.
Petrol prices are reviewed every February and August by the Finance Ministry.

Earlier this year the government slashed a surcharge on the companies by 50 percent after complaints of losses because of fluctuations of the dollar against the Cyprus pound. Companies failed to win government agreement for an increase in retail prices.
The surcharge, cut to four cents from eight cents for every litre sold, is channelled to the Cyprus electricity authority and the defence fund.

"The four cents reduction did not cover our damage...now with the new price increases there is a larger deficit," said the source. He said there was a $1.6 million loss on each crude shipment, which arrive in Cyprus twice a month.
